:::{#def-average-fit}
#### Average fit

Let $\fitproc$ be a [fitting procedure](#def-fitting-procedure),
and let $\trainset$ be a random [training set](#def-training-set).
The **average fit** of $\fitproc$ at a covariate value $\predvar$
is the prediction $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$ averaged over every training set it might have been fitted to:

$$
\avgfitf{\predvar} \eqdef \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}.
$$ {#eq-average-fit}

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

The average fit is not a prediction anyone ever holds,
because an analysis has one training set, not the whole distribution of them.
It is a reference point for measuring how far the predictions are
from the [mean function](#def-mean-function) and from each other.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-average-fit}
#### Computing the average fit

Suppose the predictions $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$ at $\predvar$
take the values $9$, $11$ and $13$ with equal probability.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\avgfitf{\predvar} &= \frac{9 + 11 + 13}{3} \\
&= 11.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
